_doc: HEAVY website_review run that exercises the path the plain website_review_happy_path deliberately avoids: REDESIGN VARIANT FAN-OUT against a TALL real page. `brief.redesign_styles` is a list (not the scalar `redesign_style`), which the website_redesign stage forwards as `styles=` to html_render_service, triggering per-style variant generation + a Chromium screenshot of each generated redesign AND a capture of the original. That variant + full-page combination was the live OOM source the html_render_service rearchitecture (durable claim-queue + MinIO + browser pool + 8000px height cap + replicas=2/HPA) was built to survive — but the only OTHER post-promote E2E hits example.com with no variants, so the dangerous path had no continuous coverage. Target is a content-rich, extremely-stable Wikipedia article (real external fetch, like example.com in the lean scenario) that is genuinely tall (~thousands of px) rather than example.com's ~600px stub — but DELIBERATELY a shorter article than the enormous `/Typography` it used to point at, to keep the heavy path inside the website_redesign.wait budget. The website_redesign stage now also requests `screenshot_viewports=[desktop]` (the 16:9 after act + compile._prefer_desktop only ever use the desktop shot), so each variant renders one viewport instead of three. `expect_stage_assertions` proves the redesign actually produced multiple distinct screenshots — terminal `completed` alone would not catch a regression that returns an empty `visuals` list. pause_after_stages:[] runs straight to `completed` through the standard script/record/compile/growth chain. Heavier than the lean scenario by design; deadline/timeout in the workflow matrix are widened accordingly.

project.title: Wikipedia Web typography — multi-variant redesign critique

brief.audience: frontend designers evaluating IA on a dense content page
redesign_styles: bold editorial, large serif headlines, dark theme, single accent
minimal swiss grid, generous whitespace, restrained palette
